title.zh: 卷六十五 列傳第二十五 吉翰 劉道產 杜驥 申恬
title.en: Volume 65 Biographies 25: Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, Shen Tian
title.raw: 卷六十五 列傳第二十五 吉翰 劉道產 杜驥 申恬 Volume 65 Biographies 25: Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, Shen Tian

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十五 吉翰 劉道產 杜驥 申恬

translations.literal: Biographies 25: Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, Shen Tian
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 25: Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, and Shen Tian

sentences.zh: 吉翰，字休文，馮翊池陽人也。

translations.literal: Ji Han, styled Xiuwen, was a man of Chiyang in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Han, whose style name was Xiuwen, came from Chiyang in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 初為龍驤將軍道憐參軍，隨府轉征虜左軍參軍，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At first he was a staff officer under the Dragon-soaring General Dao Lian; he followed the headquarters and was transferred to Left Army staff officer of the General Who Subdues Barbarians, then to Supernumerary Master of Writing in the Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary office.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a staff officer under the Dragon-soaring General Dao Lian, then moved with the headquarters to become Left Army staff officer to the General Who Subdues Barbarians and later Supernumerary Master of Writing in the Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary office.

sentences.zh: 隨道憐北征廣固，賜爵建城縣五等男。

translations.literal: He followed Dao Lian on the northern campaign against Guanggu and was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Baron of Jiancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: When Dao Lian marched north against Guanggu, Han accompanied him and received the fifth-rank barony of Jiancheng County.

sentences.zh: 轉道憐驃騎中兵參軍，從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Central Army staff officer under Dao Lian as Rapid Cavalry General and to Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Central Army staff officer to Dao Lian as Rapid Cavalry General and Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 為將佐十餘年，清謹剛正，甚為高祖所知賞。

translations.literal: For more than ten years as a military aide he was pure, careful, and upright, and was greatly known and rewarded by the Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years as a military aide he was scrupulous and upright, and Emperor Wu came to know and value him highly.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，轉道憐太尉司馬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he was transferred to Grand Marshal staff officer under Dao Lian.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu he became Grand Marshal staff officer under Dao Lian.

sentences.zh: 時太祖經略河南，以翰為持節、監司、雍、并三州諸軍事、司州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: At that time the Taizu was planning operations south of the Yellow River and appointed Han as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in Si, Yong, and Bing provinces, and Inspector of Si Province, his general's title remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wen was planning operations south of the Yellow River, Han was made Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Si, Yong, and Bing, and Inspector of Si Province, retaining his former general's rank.

sentences.zh: 會前鋒諸軍到彥之等敗退，明年，復為司徒司馬，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the vanguard armies under Dao Yanzhi and others were defeated and withdrew, the next year he again became Grand Minister of Education staff officer, his general's title as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the vanguard under Dao Yanzhi and others was defeated and withdrew, the following year he was again made staff officer to the Grand Minister of Education, with his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 其年，又假節、監徐、兗二州、豫州之梁郡諸軍事、徐州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: That same year he was also given acting staff authority, supervision of military affairs in Xu and Yan provinces and Liang commandery in Yu Province, and the post of Inspector of Xu Province, his general's title as before.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was also granted acting staff authority, supervision of military affairs in Xu and Yan and Liang commandery in Yu, and the inspectorship of Xu, again keeping his former general's rank.

sentences.zh: 時有死罪囚，典籤意欲活之，因翰入關齎呈其事。

translations.literal: At the time there was a prisoner under sentence of death; the clerk intended to save his life and, when Han entered the pass, brought in and presented the matter.
translations.idiomatic: There was then a prisoner condemned to death whom the clerk wished to spare; when Han entered the pass, the clerk brought in the case and presented it to him.

sentences.zh: 翰省訖，語「今且去，明可便呈」。

translations.literal: When Han had reviewed it he said, "Go for now; tomorrow you may present it formally."
translations.idiomatic: Han read it through and told him, "Leave for now—you may present it properly tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 明旦，典籤不敢復入，呼之乃來。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day the clerk did not dare enter again and came only when summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the clerk did not dare come in again until Han called for him.

sentences.zh: 取昨所呈事視訖，謂之曰：「卿意當欲宥此囚死命。

translations.literal: He took the matter presented yesterday, looked it over, and said to him: "You surely mean to spare this prisoner's life."
translations.idiomatic: He took up yesterday's petition, read it through, and said, "You mean to spare this man's life."

sentences.zh: 昨於齋坐見其事，亦有心活之。

translations.literal: Yesterday, seated in abstinence, I saw this matter and also had a mind to let him live.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, while I was fasting in my quarters, I saw this case and was inclined to let him live as well.

sentences.zh: 但此囚罪重，不可全貸，既欲加恩，卿便當代任其罪。

translations.literal: But this prisoner's crime is grave and cannot be wholly pardoned; since you wish to show favor, you must bear his guilt in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: But the man's crime is grave and cannot be wholly forgiven; if you wish to show him mercy, you must answer for his guilt yourself.

sentences.zh: 」因命左右收典籤付獄殺之，原此囚生命。

translations.literal: " He then ordered his attendants to seize the clerk, hand him to the prison, and execute him, and pardoned the prisoner's life.
translations.idiomatic: " He then had his attendants seize the clerk, send him to prison, and put him to death, while sparing the condemned man.

sentences.zh: 其刑政如此，其下畏服，莫敢犯禁。

translations.literal: His criminal administration was like this; those below feared and submitted, and none dared violate prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his way with law and punishment; his subordinates feared and obeyed him, and none dared break the rules.

sentences.zh: 明年卒官，時年六十。

translations.literal: The next year he died in office, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died in office at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 追贈征虜將軍，持節、監、刺史如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the General Who Subdues Barbarians, with Bearer of the Staff, supervisor, and inspector titles as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Subdues Barbarians, with his staff, supervisory, and inspectorial titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 劉道產，彭城呂人，太尉諮議參軍簡之子也。

translations.literal: Liu Daochan was a man of Lü in Pengcheng, son of Jian, a staff officer in the Grand Marshal's advisory office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daochan came from Lü in Pengcheng and was the son of Jian, advisory staff officer to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 簡之事在弟子康祖傳。

translations.literal: Jian's affairs are in the biography of his younger brother's son Kangzu.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's career is recorded in the biography of his nephew Kangzu.

sentences.zh: 道產初為輔國參軍，無錫令，在縣有能名。

translations.literal: Daochan at first was a staff officer of the State-supporting General and magistrate of Wuxi; in the county he had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Daochan first served as staff officer to the State-supporting General and as magistrate of Wuxi, where he earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 高祖版為中軍行參軍，又為道憐驃騎參軍，襲父爵晉安縣五等侯。

translations.literal: The Gaozu appointed him by commission as Central Army acting staff officer and also as staff officer under Dao Lian as Rapid Cavalry General; he inherited his father's fifth-rank Marquisate of Jin'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu commissioned him Central Army acting staff officer and staff officer to Dao Lian as Rapid Cavalry General, and he inherited his father's fifth-rank marquisate of Jin'an County.

sentences.zh: 廣州群盜因刺史謝道欣死為寇，攻沒州城，道憐加道產振武將軍南討，會始興謙之已平廣州，道產未至而反。

translations.literal: Bandits in Guangzhou, taking advantage of the death of Inspector Xie Daoxin, became raiders and captured the prefectural city; Dao Lian added Daochan as General Who Quells Martial Foes for a southern campaign, but Qianzhi of Shixing had already pacified Guangzhou before Daochan arrived, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzhou bandits turned to raiding after Inspector Xie Daoxin died and seized the prefectural city, Dao Lian gave Daochan the title General Who Quells Martial Foes and sent him south; but Qianzhi of Shixing had already pacified Guangzhou before Daochan arrived, so he turned back.

sentences.zh: 元年，除寧遠將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the first year he was dismissed to the post of General of Distant Pacification and Grand Warden of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of his reign he was appointed General of Distant Pacification and concurrent grand warden of Baxi and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 郡人黃公生、任肅之、張石之等竝譙縱餘燼，與姻親侯攬、羅奧等招引白水氐，規欲為亂。

translations.literal: Men of the commandery such as Huang Gongsheng, Ren Suzhi, and Zhang Shizhi were all embers left from Qiao Zong's rebellion; with affinal kin Hou Lan, Luo Ao, and others they drew in the Baishui Di and plotted disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Local men Huang Gongsheng, Ren Suzhi, and Zhang Shizhi were remnants of Qiao Zong's revolt; with relatives by marriage Hou Lan, Luo Ao, and others they rallied the Baishui Di and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 道產誅公生等二十一家，宥其餘黨。

translations.literal: Daochan executed Gongsheng and twenty other clans and pardoned the rest of the faction.
translations.idiomatic: Daochan executed Gongsheng and twenty other clans and pardoned the remaining conspirators.

sentences.zh: 還為彭城王義康驃騎中兵參軍。

translations.literal: On his return he became Central Army staff officer under Prince of Pengcheng Yikang as Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he became Central Army staff officer to Prince of Pengcheng Yikang as Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，督梁、南秦二州諸軍事、寧遠將軍、西戎校尉、梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he supervised military affairs in Liang and Nanqin provinces, as General of Distant Pacification, Colonel of the Western Rong, and Inspector of the two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia he was put in charge of military affairs in Liang and Nanqin as General of Distant Pacification, Colonel of the Western Rong, and inspector of both provinces.

sentences.zh: 在州有惠化，關中流民，前後出漢川歸之者甚多。

translations.literal: In the province he had benevolent transformation; displaced people from within the passes, before and after, came out of the Han River region to submit to him in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: His rule in the province was benevolent, and many displaced people from within the passes came out of the Han River region to join him.

sentences.zh: 六年，道產表置隴西、宋康二郡以領之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Daochan memorialized to establish the two commanderies of Longxi and Songkang to administer them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Daochan petitioned to establish the commanderies of Longxi and Songkang to govern the new settlers.

sentences.zh: 七年，徵為後軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned as Rear Army General.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was recalled to court as Rear Army General.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷竟陵王義宣左將軍諮議參軍，仍為持節、督雍、梁、南秦三州、荊州之南陽、竟陵、順陽、襄陽、新野、隨六郡諸軍事、寧遠將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史、襄陽太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to advisory staff officer under Prince of Jingling Yixuan as Left General and at the same time made Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Yong, Liang, and Nanqin and six commanderies in Jing Province, General of Distant Pacification, Colonel Who Pacifies the Man, Inspector of Yong, and Grand Warden of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became advisory staff officer to Prince of Jingling Yixuan as Left General, while also receiving the staff, supervision of military affairs in Yong, Liang, and Nanqin and six Jing commanderies, the title General of Distant Pacification, the colonelcy Who Pacifies the Man, the inspectorship of Yong, and the grand wardenship of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 善於臨民，在雍部政績尤著，蠻夷前後叛戾不受化者，竝皆順服，悉出緣沔為居。

translations.literal: Skilled in facing the people, in the Yong region his administrative achievements were especially marked; Man and Yi who before and after had been rebellious and would not accept civilization all submitted, and all came out to settle along the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in governing the people, he achieved his greatest success in Yong; tribes that had long refused assimilation all submitted and moved down to settle along the Han River.

sentences.zh: 百姓樂業，民戶豐贍，由此有《襄陽樂歌》，自道產始也。

translations.literal: The common people were glad in their occupations and households were rich and full; because of this there was the "Xiangyang Songs of Joy," beginning with Daochan.
translations.idiomatic: The people prospered in their work and households grew wealthy, and from this time came the "Xiangyang Songs of Joy," which began with Daochan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year his title was advanced to State-supporting General.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year his rank was raised to State-supporting General.

sentences.zh: 十九年卒，追贈征虜將軍，諡曰襄侯。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died; posthumously he was given General Who Subdues Barbarians, with the posthumous title Marquis Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year and was posthumously made General Who Subdues Barbarians with the posthumous title Marquis Xiang.

sentences.zh: 道產惠澤被於西土，及喪還，諸蠻皆備衰絰，號哭追送，至於沔口。

translations.literal: Daochan's benevolent favor spread over the western lands; when the coffin returned, all the tribes put on mourning hemp and wailed in pursuit, as far as the mouth of the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Daochan's kindness had spread throughout the west, and when his coffin was brought home every tribe donned mourning dress and wailed in procession as far as the Han River mouth.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史衡陽王義季啟太祖曰：「故輔國將軍劉道產患背癰，疾遂不救。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Province, Prince of Hengyang Yiji, reported to the Taizu: "The late State-supporting General Liu Daochan suffered a carbuncle on the back; the illness could not be cured."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hengyang Yiji, Inspector of Jing, reported to Emperor Wen: "The late State-supporting General Liu Daochan developed a carbuncle on his back and could not be saved."

sentences.zh: 道產自鎮漢南，境接凶寇，政績既著，威懷兼舉。

translations.literal: Since Daochan garrisoned the south of the Han, his border adjoined fierce enemies; his administrative achievements were already marked, and both authority and kindness were exercised together.
translations.idiomatic: Since garrisoning the Han south, where his border faced fierce enemies, he had won outstanding achievements and combined stern authority with gentle persuasion.

sentences.zh: 年時猶可，方宣其用，奄至殞沒，傷怨特深。

translations.literal: His years were still serviceable and he was just about to display his use; suddenly he fell and perished—the grief and resentment are especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: He was still in his prime and ready to do more when death struck suddenly, leaving grief and resentment unusually deep.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖懷，愍惜兼至。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Your Sagely Heart's pity and regret reach together.
translations.idiomatic: I trust Your Majesty will feel both pity and deep regret."

sentences.zh: 」長子延孫，別有傳。

translations.literal: " His eldest son Yansun has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yansun has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 延孫弟延熙，因延孫之廕，大明中，為司徒右長史，黃門郎，臨海、義興太守。

translations.literal: Yansun's younger brother Yanxi, through Yansun's inherited privilege, in the Daming era was Right Chief Clerk of the Grand Minister of Education, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, and Grand Warden of Linhai and Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun's younger brother Yanxi, benefiting from Yansun's privilege, served in the Daming era as Right Chief Clerk to the Grand Minister of Education, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, and grand warden of Linhai and Yixing.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，與四方同反，伏誅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he rebelled together with the four quarters and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi he joined the widespread revolt and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 道產弟道錫，巴西、梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: Daochan's younger brother Daoxi was Grand Warden of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Daochan's younger brother Daoxi served as grand warden of Baxi and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十八年，為氐寇所攻，道錫保城退敵，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia he was attacked by Di raiders; Daoxi held the city and repelled the enemy, and the Taizu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia Di raiders attacked him; Daoxi held the city and drove them off, and Emperor Wen commended him.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「前者兵寇攻逼，邊情波駭，廣威將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守劉道錫，將率文武，盡心固守，保全之績，厥效可書。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: "Recently military raiders pressed the attack and border feelings were shaken with alarm. General of Broad Prestige, Grand Warden of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong Liu Daoxi led civil and military officials and devoted himself to firm defense; the achievement of preservation can be recorded."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "When raiders recently pressed the border and alarm spread, Liu Daoxi, General of Broad Prestige and grand warden of Baxi and Zitong, led his civil and military staff in a resolute defense, and his success in preserving the city deserves to be recorded."

sentences.zh: 可冠軍。

translations.literal: He may be made Champion.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be made Champion General."

sentences.zh: 諮議參軍、前建威將軍、晉壽太守申坦，孤城弱眾，厲志致果，死傷參半，壯氣不衰，雖力屈陷沒，在誠宜甄。

translations.literal: Advisory staff officer, former General Who Establishes Might, Grand Warden of Jinshou Shen Tian, with a lone city and weak forces, stiffened his will to achieve results; casualties were half, yet his bold spirit did not decline; though strength was exhausted and he fell, in sincerity he should be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Advisory staff officer Shen Tian, former General Who Establishes Might and grand warden of Jinshou, held a lone city with few troops, yet fought with fierce resolve; though half his men were killed or wounded and his strength failed until the city fell, his loyalty deserves recognition.

sentences.zh: 可建威將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: He may be made General Who Establishes Might and Grand Warden of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be made General Who Establishes Might and grand warden of Baxi and Zitong."

sentences.zh: 」初，氐寇至，城內眾寡，道錫募吏民守城，復租布二十年。

translations.literal: " At first, when the Di raiders arrived, forces within the city were few; Daoxi recruited officials and people to defend the city and remitted rent and cloth levies for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di first attacked, the garrison was weak; Daoxi recruited officials and townspeople to defend the walls and promised a twenty-year remission of rent and cloth taxes.

sentences.zh: 及賊退，朝議：「賊雖攻城，一戰便走，聽依本要，於事為優。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, the court debated: "Though the bandits besieged the city, they fled after one battle; let the original promise stand—this is preferable in affairs."
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew, court opinion held: "The raiders fled after a single engagement, so the original promise should stand—that is the better course."

sentences.zh: 」右衛將軍沈演之、丹陽尹羊玄保、後軍長史范曄竝謂：「宜隨功勞裁量，不可全用本誓，多者不得過十年。

translations.literal: " Right Guards General Shen Yanzhi, Intendant of Danyang Yang Xuanbao, and Rear Army Chief Clerk Fan Ye all said: "It should be measured according to merit and toil; the original oath cannot be used in full—the maximum should not exceed ten years."
translations.idiomatic: Right Guards General Shen Yanzhi, Intendant of Danyang Yang Xuanbao, and Rear Army Chief Clerk Fan Ye all argued: "The remission should match actual merit; the full pledge cannot be honored, and no grant should exceed ten years."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted their view.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遷揚烈將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to General of the Uplifted Blaze and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was made General of the Uplifted Blaze and Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，坐貪縱過度，自杖治中荀齊文垂死，乘輿出城行，與阿尼同載，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, on account of excessive greed and indulgence, he himself beat his Chief Clerk Xun Qiwen nearly to death, went out of the city in his carriage for a pleasure outing, and rode in the same carriage with a Buddhist nun; he was impeached by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was impeached for gross greed and license: he had beaten his chief clerk Xun Qiwen nearly to death, taken his carriage out of the city for pleasure, and ridden with a Buddhist nun in the same coach.

sentences.zh: 值赦，明年散徵。

translations.literal: An amnesty intervened; the next year he was dismissed and summoned.
translations.idiomatic: He benefited from an amnesty, but the following year he was dismissed and recalled.

sentences.zh: 又以赦後餘贓，收下廷尉，被宥病卒。

translations.literal: Again, on account of remaining guilt after the amnesty, he was taken in by the Court Commandant; he was pardoned and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was then handed to the Court Commandant on remaining charges after the amnesty, was pardoned, and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 杜驥，字度世，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Du Ji, styled Dushi, was a man of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji, whose style name was Dushi, came from Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 高祖預，晉征南將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yu was Jin General Who Subdues the South.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yu had been Jin General Who Subdues the South.

sentences.zh: 曾祖耽，避難河西，因仕張氏。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Dan fled to Hexi for refuge and therefore served the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Dan took refuge in Hexi and entered service under the Zhang regime.

sentences.zh: 苻堅平涼州，父祖始還關中。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian pacified Liang Province, his father and grandfather first returned within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian conquered Liangzhou, his father and grandfather returned to the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 兄坦，頗涉史傳。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tan was fairly versed in historical writings.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Tan was well read in history.

sentences.zh: 高祖征長安，席捲隨從南還。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu campaigned against Chang'an, they swept along in his train and returned south.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu marched on Chang'an, they joined his advance and returned south with him.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉中，任遇甚厚，歷後軍將軍，龍驤將軍，青、冀二州刺史，南平王鑠右將軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era under the Taizu, Tan received very generous appointments, serving as Rear Army General, Dragon-soaring General, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, and Right General staff officer under Prince of Nanping Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen in the Yuanjia era Tan enjoyed exceptional favor, serving as Rear Army General, Dragon-soaring General, inspector of Qing and Ji, and staff officer to Prince of Nanping Shuo as Right General.

sentences.zh: 晚度北人，朝廷常以傖荒遇之，雖復人才可施，每為清塗所隔，坦以此慨然。

translations.literal: As northerners who had crossed south late, the court always treated them as crude outsiders; though their talent could still be employed, they were repeatedly blocked from the pure path, and Tan was indignant at this.
translations.idiomatic: As late-arriving northerners, they were commonly treated at court as crude outsiders; though their talents were usable, the established elite kept them from high office, and Tan brooded over it.

sentences.zh: 嘗與太祖言及史籍，上曰：「金日磾忠孝淳深，漢朝莫及，恨今世無復如此輩人。

translations.literal: Once, speaking with the Taizu about historical records, the Emperor said: "Jin Midi's loyalty and filial piety were pure and deep; the Han court could not match him—I regret that today there are no longer men of this sort."
translations.idiomatic: Once, discussing history with Emperor Wen, the Emperor said, "Jin Midi's loyalty and filial devotion were profound beyond anything the Han could match; I regret that men like him no longer exist today."

sentences.zh: 」坦曰：「日磾之美，誠如聖詔。

translations.literal: " Tan said: "Midi's excellence is indeed as Your Sagely Edict states."
translations.idiomatic: Tan replied, "Your Majesty is right about Midi's excellence."

sentences.zh: 假使生乎今世，養馬不暇，豈辦見知。

translations.literal: If he were born in the present age, he would have no leisure beyond tending horses—how could he win recognition?
translations.idiomatic: But if he were born in our day he would have no time beyond tending horses—how would he ever be noticed?

sentences.zh: 」上變色曰：「卿何量朝廷之薄也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor changed color and said: "How do you measure the court so meanly?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's face darkened. "Why do you judge the court so harshly?"

sentences.zh: 」坦曰：「請以臣言之。

translations.literal: " Tan said: "Allow me to speak from my own case."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "Let me speak from my own case."

sentences.zh: 臣本中華高族，亡曾祖晉氏喪亂，播遷涼土，世葉相承，不殞其舊。

translations.literal: I was originally of a lofty clan of the Central States; my deceased great-great-grandfather, in the Jin disorder, was scattered to the Liang lands, yet generation after generation succeeded one another without extinguishing the old standing.
translations.idiomatic: I come from an eminent Central Plains family; my great-great-grandfather fled the Jin collapse to the Liang region, yet our line endured generation after generation without losing its standing.

sentences.zh: 直以南度不早，便以荒傖賜隔。

translations.literal: Simply because we crossed south late, we are set apart as crude outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet simply because we crossed south late, we are dismissed as crude outsiders.

sentences.zh: 日磾胡人，身為牧圉，便超入內侍，齒列名賢。

translations.literal: Midi was a barbarian; his person was a horse-keeper, yet he was promoted straight into inner attendance and ranked among famed worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Midi was a foreigner who tended horses, yet he was raised straight into the inner service and ranked among celebrated men.

sentences.zh: 聖朝雖復拔才，臣恐未必能也。

translations.literal: Though the sagely court again selects talent, I fear it may not necessarily be able to do so.
translations.idiomatic: Your dynasty may claim to promote talent, but I doubt it would do the same today."

sentences.zh: 」上默然。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 北土舊法，問疾必遣子弟。

translations.literal: By the old custom of the northern lands, when inquiring after illness one must send sons or younger kin.
translations.idiomatic: In the north it was customary to send a son or younger relative when calling on the sick.

sentences.zh: 驥年十三，父使候同郡韋華。

translations.literal: Ji was thirteen when his father sent him to call on Wei Hua of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji was thirteen his father sent him to inquire after Wei Hua of the same commandery.

sentences.zh: 華子玄有高名，見而異之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Hua's son Xuan had a high reputation; seeing Ji he was struck by him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Hua's son Xuan was highly esteemed; struck by the boy, he gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 桂陽公義真鎮長安，辟為州主簿，後為義真車騎行參軍，員外散騎侍郎，江夏王義恭撫軍刑獄參軍，尚書都官郎，長沙王義欣後軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Duke of Guiyang Yizhen garrisoned Chang'an he recruited Ji as provincial chief clerk; later he was Yizhen's acting staff officer of the Chariots and Cavalry, Supernumerary Master of Writing in the Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary office, criminal affairs staff officer under Prince of Jiangxia Yigong as Pacification General, Master of Writing in the Ministry of Justice, and recording staff officer under Prince of Changsha Yixin as Rear Army General.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Guiyang Yizhen held Chang'an he made Ji provincial chief clerk; later Ji served Yizhen as acting Chariots and Cavalry staff officer, Supernumerary Master of Writing at the Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary office, criminal affairs staff officer to Prince of Jiangxia Yigong as Pacification General, Master of Writing in the Ministry of Justice, and recording staff officer to Prince of Changsha Yixin as Rear Army General.

sentences.zh: 元嘉七年，隨到彥之入河南，加建武將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanjia he followed Dao Yanzhi into the region south of the Yellow River and was given the additional title General Who Establishes Martial Might.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanjia he followed Dao Yanzhi south of the Yellow River and was made General Who Establishes Martial Might.

sentences.zh: 索虜撤河南戍悉歸河北，彥之使驥守洛陽。

translations.literal: The northern enemy withdrew all garrisons south of the Yellow River back north of the river; Yanzhi had Ji guard Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern enemy pulled every garrison south of the Yellow River back north, Yanzhi left Ji to hold Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 洛陽城不治既久，又無糧食，及彥之敗退，驥欲棄城走，慮為太祖所誅。

translations.literal: Luoyang's walls had long gone unrepaired and there was no grain; when Yanzhi was defeated and withdrew, Ji wished to abandon the city and flee, fearing execution by the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's walls had long been neglected and food was gone; when Yanzhi's army collapsed and withdrew, Ji wanted to abandon the city and flee, fearing Emperor Wen would have him executed.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖平關洛，致鐘虡舊器南還，一大鐘墜洛水。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Gaozu pacified the Guan and Luo regions, he brought the old bells and ritual vessels south; one great bell fell into the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu had pacified the Guanzhong and Luoyang region he brought the old bells and ritual vessels south, and one great bell fell into the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 至是太祖遣將姚聳夫領千五百人迎致之。

translations.literal: At this time the Taizu sent the general Yao Songfu leading fifteen hundred men to welcome and bring it back.
translations.idiomatic: Now Emperor Wen sent General Yao Songfu with fifteen hundred men to recover it.

sentences.zh: 時聳夫政率所領牽鐘于洛水，驥乃誑之曰：「虜既南渡，洛城勢弱，今修理城池，竝已堅固，軍糧又足，所乏者人耳。

translations.literal: At that time Songfu was just leading his troops to haul the bell at the Luo River; Ji then deceived him, saying: "The enemy has already crossed south; Luoyang's position is weak. We have now repaired the walls and they are all firm, military grain is also sufficient—only men are lacking."
translations.idiomatic: Songfu was then hauling the bell at the Luo River when Ji deceived him, saying, "The enemy has crossed south and Luoyang is weak, but we have repaired the walls and they are sound, provisions are ample—we only lack men.

sentences.zh: 君率眾見就，共守此城，大功既立，取鐘無晚。

translations.literal: If you lead your forces to join us and we defend this city together, once the great achievement is established, recovering the bell will not be late.
translations.idiomatic: Bring your men and help hold the city; once that great deed is done, fetching the bell will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 」聳夫信之，率所領就驥。

translations.literal: " Songfu believed him and led his troops to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu believed him and marched his men to Ji.

sentences.zh: 既至，見城不可守，又無糧食，於是引眾去。

translations.literal: When they arrived he saw the city could not be held and there was no grain, and so led his troops away.
translations.idiomatic: Once there he saw the city could not be held and there was no food, so he led his troops away.

sentences.zh: 驥亦委城南奔，白太祖曰：「本欲以死固守，姚聳夫及城便走，人情沮敗，不可復禁。

translations.literal: Ji also abandoned the city and fled south, reporting to the Taizu: "I originally intended to hold firm unto death, but Yao Songfu reached the city and at once fled; men's spirits were broken and could no longer be restrained."
translations.idiomatic: Ji too abandoned the city and fled south, telling Emperor Wen, "I meant to die defending the place, but Yao Songfu fled as soon as he arrived; morale collapsed and could not be restored."

sentences.zh: 」上大怒，使建威將軍鄭順之殺聳夫於壽陽。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was greatly angry and had General Who Establishes Might Zheng Shunzhi execute Songfu at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and had General Who Establishes Might Zheng Shunzhi execute Songfu at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 聳夫，吳興武康人。

translations.literal: Songfu was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 勇果有氣力，宋世偏裨小將莫及。

translations.literal: Brave, resolute, and strong, among the Song age's junior commanders and petty generals none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and powerful, no junior officer of the Song matched him.

sentences.zh: 始隨到彥之北伐，與虜遇，聳夫手斬托跋燾叔父英文特勒首，燾以馬百匹贖之。

translations.literal: At first he followed Dao Yanzhi on the northern campaign; meeting the enemy, Songfu with his own hand cut off the head of Tuo Ba Tao's uncle Yingwen Tele; Tao ransomed it with a hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He had first followed Dao Yanzhi north, and in battle with the enemy personally cut off the head of Tuo Ba Tao's uncle Yingwen Tele; Tao paid a ransom of a hundred horses for it.

sentences.zh: 以驥為通直郎，射聲校尉，世祖征虜諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Ji was made Palace Cadet of Direct Communication, Colonel of the Archers, and advisory staff officer under the Shizu as General Who Subdues Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was made Palace Cadet of Direct Communication, Colonel of the Archers, and advisory staff officer to Emperor Xiaowu as General Who Subdues Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 十七年，出督青、冀二州、徐州之東莞、東安二郡諸軍事、寧遠將軍、青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he went out to supervise military affairs in Qing and Ji provinces and the two commanderies of Dongguan and Dong'an in Xu Province, as General of Distant Pacification and Inspector of the two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was sent out to supervise military affairs in Qing and Ji and the Xu commanderies of Dongguan and Dong'an as General of Distant Pacification and inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 在任八年，惠化著於齊土。

translations.literal: In office eight years, his benevolent transformation was marked in the Qi lands.
translations.idiomatic: During eight years in office his benevolent rule became renowned throughout Qi.

sentences.zh: 自義熙至於宋末，刺史唯羊穆之及驥，為吏民所稱詠。

translations.literal: From Yixi down to the end of Song, among inspectors only Yang Muzhi and Ji were praised and sung by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yixi era to the end of the Song, only Yang Muzhi and Ji among provincial inspectors were praised and celebrated by officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，徵左軍將軍，兄坦代為刺史，北土以為榮焉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was summoned as Left Army General; his elder brother Tan replaced him as inspector, and the northern lands regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was recalled as Left Army General while his brother Tan took over as inspector—a mark of honor in the north.

sentences.zh: 坦長子琬為員外散騎侍郎，太祖嘗有函詔敕坦，琬輒開視。

translations.literal: Tan's eldest son Wan was Supernumerary Master of Writing in the Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary office; the Taizu once had a sealed edict instructing Tan, and Wan at once opened and looked at it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's eldest son Wan served as Supernumerary Master of Writing at the Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary office; when Emperor Wen once sent Tan a sealed edict, Wan opened and read it.

sentences.zh: 信未發又追取之，敕函已發，大相推檢。

translations.literal: Before the letter was sent it was pursued and taken back; the sealed order had already been opened, and there was a great mutual investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger was recalled before the letter left, but the seal had already been broken, and a major inquiry followed.

sentences.zh: 丞都答云：「諸郎開視。

translations.literal: The chief clerk of the commandery answered: "All the young gentlemen opened and looked."
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk answered, "All the young gentlemen opened it."

sentences.zh: 」上遣主書詰責，驥答曰：「開函是臣第四子季文，伏待刑坐。

translations.literal: " The Emperor sent a chief clerk to question and blame him; Ji answered: "The one who opened the seal was my fourth son Jiwen; I submit and await punishment."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent an official to question him; Ji replied, "My fourth son Jiwen opened the seal; I await punishment."

sentences.zh: 」上特原不問。

translations.literal: " The Emperor especially pardoned him and did not inquire further.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor specially pardoned him and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-seventh year at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 長子長文，早卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Changwen died young.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Changwen died young.

sentences.zh: 第五子幼文，薄於行。

translations.literal: His fifth son Youwen was shallow in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth son Youwen was morally deficient.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，以軍功為驍騎將軍，封邵陽縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taizong era, on account of military achievement he was made Valiant Cavalry General, enfeoffed as Baron of Shaoyang County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Ming's reign he was made Valiant Cavalry General for military merit and enfeoffed as Baron of Shaoyang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋坐巧佞奪爵。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of crafty flattery, his title was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he lost his title for crafty flattery.

sentences.zh: 後以發太尉廬江王禕謀反事，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later, for exposing the rebellion plot of Grand Marshal, Prince of Lujiang Yi, he was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for exposing Grand Marshal Prince of Lujiang Yi's plot to rebel, he was made Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 出為輔國將軍、梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as State-supporting General and Inspector of the two provinces of Liang and Nanqin.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as State-supporting General and inspector of Liang and Nanqin.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元徽中，為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor in the Yuanhui era he was Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor in the Yuanhui era he served as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 幼文所蒞貪橫，家累千金，女伎數十人，絲竹晝夜不絕，與沈勃、孫超之居止接近，常相從，又竝與阮佃夫厚善。

translations.literal: Where Youwen governed he was greedy and overbearing; his household amassed thousands in gold; he had several tens of female performers; string and bamboo music never ceased day or night; he lived close to Shen Bo and Sun Chaozhi and constantly accompanied them, and both were also on close terms with Ruan Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: In office Youwen was greedy and domineering; his household held thousands in gold, he kept dozens of female musicians, and music sounded day and night; he lived near Shen Bo and Sun Chaozhi, kept their company constantly, and all three were close to Ruan Tianfu.

sentences.zh: 佃夫死，廢帝深疾之。

translations.literal: When Tianfu died, the Deposed Emperor deeply hated them.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianfu's death the Deposed Emperor came to hate them deeply.

sentences.zh: 帝微行夜出，輒在幼文門牆之間，聽其弦管，積久轉不能平，於是自率宿衛兵誅幼文、勃、超之等。

translations.literal: The Emperor went out incognito at night and would be by Youwen's gate and wall listening to his strings and pipes; as this built up over time he could not calm himself, and so personally led the palace guard to execute Youwen, Bo, Chaozhi, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would slip out at night and linger by Youwen's house to listen to the music; resentment built until he led the palace guard himself to kill Youwen, Bo, Chaozhi, and the others.

sentences.zh: 幼文兄叔文為長水校尉，及諸子侄在京邑方鎮者竝誅。

translations.literal: Youwen's elder brother Shuwen was Colonel of the Long River; all sons and nephews in the capital region or in provincial posts were likewise executed.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen's brother Shuwen, Colonel of the Long River, and all sons and nephews in the capital or in provincial posts were executed as well.

sentences.zh: 唯幼文兄季文、弟希文等數人，逃亡得免。

translations.literal: Only Youwen's elder brother Jiwen, younger brother Xiwen, and several others fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Only Youwen's brother Jiwen, his younger brother Xiwen, and a few others escaped by flight.

sentences.zh: 申恬，字公休，魏郡魏人也。

translations.literal: Shen Tian, styled Gongxiu, was a man of Wei in Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tian, whose style name was Gongxiu, came from Wei in Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖鍾，為石虎司徒。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhong was Minister of Education under Shi Hu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhong had been Minister of Education under Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 高祖平廣固，恬父宣、宣從父兄永皆得歸國，竝以幹用見知。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu pacified Guanggu, Tian's father Xuan and Xuan's father's younger brother Yong were both able to return to the state and were both known for practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu pacified Guanggu, Tian's father Xuan and Xuan's cousin Yong both returned to Song service and were valued for their competence.

sentences.zh: 永歷青、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: Yong served as Inspector of Qing and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had served as inspector of Qing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu ascended the throne, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Yong was made Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 宣，太祖元嘉初，亦歷兗、青二州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan, at the beginning of Yuanjia under the Taizu, also served in turn as Inspector of Yan and Qing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, early in Emperor Wen's Yuanjia reign, likewise served as inspector of Yan and Qing.

sentences.zh: 恬兄謨，與朱脩之守滑臺，為虜所沒，後得叛還。

translations.literal: Tian's elder brother Mo, together with Zhu Xiuzhi, defended Huatai and was overrun by the enemy; later he was able to defect and return.
translations.idiomatic: Tian's elder brother Mo had defended Huatai with Zhu Xiuzhi, was captured by the enemy, and later defected back to Song.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，為竟陵太守。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era he was Grand Warden of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanjia he served as grand warden of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 恬初為驃騎道憐長兼行參軍。

translations.literal: Tian at first was senior acting staff officer under Dao Lian as Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Tian began as senior acting staff officer to Dao Lian as Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，拜東宮殿中將軍，度還臺。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu ascended the throne, he was appointed Palace General of the Eastern Palace and then transferred back to the central government.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Tian was made Palace General of the Eastern Palace, then returned to the central government.

sentences.zh: 直省十載，不請休息。

translations.literal: He served in direct attendance for ten years without requesting rest.
translations.idiomatic: He stood palace duty for ten years without asking for leave.

sentences.zh: 轉員外散騎侍郎，出為綏遠將軍、下邳太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supernumerary Master of Writing in the Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary office and went out as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Grand Warden of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: He became Supernumerary Master of Writing at the Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary office, then was sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distance and grand warden of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 轉在北海，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Beihai and given the additional title General of Distant Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Beihai with the additional rank of General of Distant Pacification.

sentences.zh: 所至皆有政績。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Every post he held showed solid administrative results.

sentences.zh: 又為北譙、梁二郡太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He again served as Grand Warden of the two commanderies of Beiqiao and Liang, his general's title as before.
translations.idiomatic: He then served as grand warden of Beiqiao and Liang, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 郡境邊接任榛，屢被寇抄。

translations.literal: The commandery's border adjoined Ren Zhen's territory and was repeatedly raided.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery bordered the territory of the bandit Ren Zhen and suffered repeated raids.

sentences.zh: 恬到，密知賊來，仍伏兵要害，出其不意，悉皆禽殄。

translations.literal: When Tian arrived he secretly learned the bandits were coming, then laid troops in ambush at a critical point and, catching them unawares, captured and destroyed them all.
translations.idiomatic: On arriving Tian learned secretly that the bandits were coming, ambushed them at a choke point, and destroyed them by surprise.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，遷督魯、東平、濟北三郡軍事、泰山太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to supervise military affairs in the three commanderies of Lu, Dongping, and Jibei and to be Grand Warden of Taishan, his general's title as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was put in charge of military affairs in Lu, Dongping, and Jibei and made grand warden of Taishan, keeping his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 惠威兼著，吏民便之。

translations.literal: Benevolence and authority were both marked; officials and people found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: His kindness and authority were equally evident, and officials and commoners alike benefited.

sentences.zh: 臨川王義慶鎮江陵，為平西中兵參軍、河東太守。

translations.literal: When Prince of Linchuan Yiqing garrisoned Jiangling, he was Central Army staff officer of the Pacification West command and Grand Warden of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Linchuan Yiqing held Jiangling, Tian served as Central Army staff officer of the Pacify-the-West command and grand warden of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王義季代義慶，又度安西府，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Hengyang Yiji replaced Yiqing, he again crossed to the Pacification West headquarters and was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Hengyang Yiji replaced Yiqing, Tian transferred to the Pacify-the-West headquarters and was made General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 召拜太子屯騎校尉，母憂去職。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry of the Heir Apparent and left office on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and made Colonel of the Heir Apparent's Garrison Cavalry, then left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，冀州移鎮歷下，以恬督冀州、青州之濟南、樂安、太原三郡諸軍事、揚烈將軍、冀州刺史，明年，加濟南太守。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Jizhou's garrison was moved to Lixia; Tian was made supervisor of military affairs in Jizhou and the three commanderies of Jinan, Le'an, and Taiyuan in Qing Province, General of the Uplifted Blaze, and Inspector of Jizhou; the next year he was given the additional post of Grand Warden of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the Jizhou garrison moved to Lixia; Tian supervised military affairs in Jizhou and the Qing commanderies of Jinan, Le'an, and Taiyuan as General of the Uplifted Blaze and inspector of Jizhou, and the next year was also made grand warden of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 時又遷換諸郡守，恬上表曰：「伏聞朝恩當加臣濟南太守，仰惟優旨，荒心散越。

translations.literal: At that time commandery grand wardens were again being transferred and replaced; Tian submitted a memorial saying: "I bow and hear that court grace is about to add me as Grand Warden of Jinan; looking up and considering this excellent decree, my benighted heart is scattered and overwhelmed."
translations.idiomatic: When commandery grand wardens were being rotated again, Tian memorialized: "I learn that the court intends to add the grand wardenship of Jinan to my duties; I am overwhelmed by this gracious decree."

sentences.zh: 臣殃咎之餘，遭蒙逾忝，寵私罔己，復兼今授，豈其愚迷，所能上答。

translations.literal: I, a remnant of calamity and guilt, have received favor beyond my deserts; private grace knows no limit, and now this additional appointment is added—how could such stupidity and confusion be able to respond above?
translations.idiomatic: A man already laden with fault, I have received favor beyond my deserts; now this added appointment is more than my dull wits can repay.

sentences.zh: 臣近至止，即履行所統，究其形宜。

translations.literal: Since I recently arrived and stopped, I have at once toured what I govern and examined its terrain and suitability.
translations.idiomatic: Since my recent arrival I have toured my jurisdiction and studied its terrain.

sentences.zh: 河、濟之間，應置戍捍，其中四處，急須修立，甕口故城，又是要所，宜移太原，委以邊事。

translations.literal: Between the Yellow and Ji rivers garrisons for defense should be set; of these, four places urgently need to be built and established; the old city at Wengkou is again a critical point—it is fitting to move Taiyuan there and entrust border affairs to it.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Yellow and Ji rivers defensive posts are needed; four sites require urgent construction, and the old city at Wengkou is another key point where Taiyuan commandery should be moved and entrusted with border defense.

sentences.zh: 緣山諸邏，並得除省，防衛綏懷，利便非一。

translations.literal: The various outposts along the mountains may all be abolished and reduced; defense, pacification, and cherishing would bring more than one benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain outposts could be abolished, simplifying defense and pacification with many advantages.

sentences.zh: 呂綽誠效益著，深同臣意，百姓聞者，咸皆附說，急有同異，二三未宜。

translations.literal: Lü Chuo's loyalty and benefits are marked; he deeply agrees with my intent; common people who hear all attach themselves to the proposal—only where there are urgent differences, two or three points are not yet suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chuo has shown loyal and effective service and agrees with me deeply; the people who hear of this all support the plan, though two or three urgent points still need adjustment.

sentences.zh: 但房紹之蒞郡經年，軍民粗狎，改以帶臣，有乖永事。

translations.literal: But Fang Shaozhi has governed the commandery for years; army and people are somewhat familiar with him; to change and have me hold it concurrently goes against long-term affairs.
translations.idiomatic: But Fang Shaozhi has governed the commandery for years and won the army's and people's familiarity; replacing him with me in a concurrent post would disrupt established arrangements.

sentences.zh: 遠牽太原，於民為苦。

translations.literal: Dragging Taiyuan far away would be hardship for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Moving Taiyuan so far would burden the people.

sentences.zh: 而甕口之計，復成交互，人情非樂，容有不安。

translations.literal: Yet the Wengkou plan again creates mutual entanglement; people's feelings are not pleased, and there may be unrest.
translations.idiomatic: The Wengkou plan would also create overlapping jurisdictions, displeasing the people and inviting unrest.

sentences.zh: 疆場威刑，患不開廣，若得依先處分，公私允緝。

translations.literal: On the frontier authority and punishment fear not being broad and open; if we can follow the prior disposition, public and private affairs will be harmoniously settled.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier authority needs clarity; if the earlier arrangements are kept, public and private interests will both be served."

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 詔有司曰：「恬所陳當是事宜，近諸除授可悉停。」

translations.literal: An edict to the authorities said: "What Tian stated fits the circumstances of affairs; recent appointments and grants may all be halted."
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the ministries said, "Tian's proposals are appropriate; suspend all recent appointments."

sentences.zh: 北虜入寇，恬摧擊之，為虜所破，被徴還都。

translations.literal: The northern enemy invaded; Tian struck and pressed them but was defeated by the enemy and was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern enemy invaded, Tian attacked them but was defeated and recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，起為通直常侍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was raised as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was reappointed Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 是歲，索虜南寇，其武昌王向青州。

translations.literal: That year the northern enemy raided south; their Prince of Wuchang advanced on Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: That year the northern enemy raided south, and their Prince of Wuchang marched on Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 遣恬援東陽，因與輔國司馬、齊郡太守龐秀之保城固守。

translations.literal: Tian was sent to relieve Dongyang and, together with State-supporting General staff officer and Grand Warden of Qi Commandery Pang Xiuzhi, held the city and defended firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Tian was sent to relieve Dongyang, where he and State-supporting General staff officer Pang Xiuzhi, grand warden of Qi, held the city in a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌遣青州別駕解榮之率垣護之還援恬等，仍傍南山得入。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin sent Qing Province Vice-Prefect Xie Rongzhi leading Yuan Huzhi back to relieve Tian and the others; they still went along the southern mountains and were able to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin sent Qing Vice-Prefect Xie Rongzhi with Yuan Huzhi to relieve them; they entered by way of the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 賊朝來脅城，日晚輒退。

translations.literal: The bandits came by day to threaten the city and every evening withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy came by day to threaten the walls and withdrew each evening.

sentences.zh: 城內乃出車北門外，環塹為營，欲挑戰，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: Those inside the city then brought chariots outside the north gate, ringed the moat to make camps, and wished to offer battle; the bandits did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders then brought chariots out the north gate and ringed the moat with camps to offer battle; the enemy did not dare close in.

sentences.zh: 停五日，東過抄略清河郡及驛道南數千家，從東安、東莞出下邳。

translations.literal: After five days' halt they passed east, raiding Qinghe Commandery and several thousand households south of the post road, and went out from Dong'an and Dongguan toward Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: After five days they marched east, plundering Qinghe and thousands of households along the post road south, then left through Dong'an and Dongguan toward Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 下邳太守垣閬閉城距守，保全二千餘家。

translations.literal: Grand Warden of Xiapi Yuan Lang closed the city and resisted defense, preserving more than two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Warden of Xiapi Yuan Lang shut the gates and held out, saving more than two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 虜退，以恬為寧朔將軍、山陽太守。

translations.literal: When the enemy withdrew, Tian was made General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Warden of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew, Tian was made General Who Pacifies the North and grand warden of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 善於治民，所蒞有績。

translations.literal: Skilled in governing the people, wherever he governed he had achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in governing the people, he achieved solid results in every post.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，遷青州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the Shizu ascended the throne, he was transferred to Inspector of Qing Province, his general's title as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Tian was made inspector of Qing, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 尋加督徐州之東莞、東安二郡諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally given supervision of military affairs in the two Xu commanderies of Dongguan and Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also put in charge of military affairs in Xu's Dongguan and Dong'an commanderies.

sentences.zh: 明年，又督冀州。

translations.literal: The next year he also supervised Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he also supervised Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 齊地連歲興兵，百姓凋弊，恬初防衛邊境，勸課農桑，二三年間，遂皆優實。

translations.literal: The Qi lands had raised armies year after year and the people were depleted; when Tian first defended the border and urged farming and sericulture, within two or three years all became prosperous and full.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had suffered years of warfare and the people were exhausted; when Tian took charge of the border he promoted farming and sericulture, and within two or three years the region grew prosperous again.

sentences.zh: 性清約，頻處州郡，妻子不免饑寒，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: By nature pure and frugal, though he repeatedly held provincial and commandery posts, his wife and children did not escape hunger and cold; the age praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal by nature, he held repeated provincial posts yet his wife and children still knew hunger and cold, for which the age praised him.

sentences.zh: 進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to State-supporting General.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was raised to State-supporting General.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，遷督豫州軍事、寧朔將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian he was transferred to supervise military affairs in Yuzhou, as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian he was put in charge of Yuzhou military affairs as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，疾病徵還，於道卒，時年六十九。

translations.literal: The next year, ill, he was summoned back and died on the road, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, recalled because of illness, he died on the road at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 死之日，家無遺財。

translations.literal: On the day of his death his household had no remaining wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his household had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 子實，南譙郡太守，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Shi was Grand Warden of Nanqiao Commandery and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi, grand warden of Nanqiao, died young.

sentences.zh: 謨子元嗣，海陵、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: Mo's son Yuansi was Grand Warden of Hailing and Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's son Yuansi served as grand warden of Hailing and Guangling.

sentences.zh: 元嗣弟謙，太始初，以軍功歷軍校，官至輔國將軍、臨川內史。

translations.literal: Yuansi's younger brother Qian, at the beginning of Taishi, on account of military achievement passed through army command posts and reached the posts of State-supporting General and Interior Minister of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansi's younger brother Qian, early in Taishi, rose through army commands for military merit to State-supporting General and interior minister of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 永子坦，自巴西、梓潼遷梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Yong's son Tan was transferred from Baxi and Zitong to Inspector of the two provinces of Liang and Nanqin.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's son Tan moved from Baxi and Zitong to inspector of Liang and Nanqin.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，為世祖鎮軍諮議參軍，與王玄謨圍滑臺不克，免官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was advisory staff officer under the Shizu as Garrison Army General; with Wang Xuanmo he besieged Huatai without success and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was advisory staff officer to Emperor Xiaowu as Garrison Army General; he joined Wang Xuanmo in besieging Huatai without success and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史蕭斌板行建威將軍、濟南、平原二郡太守，復攻確磝，敗退，下歷城。

translations.literal: Inspector of Qing Province Xiao Bin commissioned him acting General Who Establishes Might and Grand Warden of the two commanderies of Jinan and Pingyuan; he again attacked Que'ao, was defeated and withdrew, and went down to Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Inspector Xiao Bin commissioned him acting General Who Establishes Might and grand warden of Jinan and Pingyuan; he attacked Que'ao again, was beaten back, and withdrew to Licheng.

sentences.zh: 蕭思話起義討元兇，假坦輔國將軍，為前鋒。

translations.literal: When Xiao Sihua raised righteous troops to punish the prime culprit, Tan was given acting State-supporting General and made vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Sihua rose to punish the usurper, Tan was made acting State-supporting General and vanguard.

sentences.zh: 世祖至新亭，坦亦進克京城。

translations.literal: When the Shizu reached Xinting, Tan also advanced and captured the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, Tan also advanced and took the capital.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，為太子右衛率，寧朔將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaojian he became Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，虜寇兗州，世祖遣太子衛率薛安都、新除東陽太守沈法系北討，至兗州，虜已去。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming the enemy raided Yan Province; the Shizu sent the Heir Apparent's Guard Commandant Xue Andu and the newly appointed Grand Warden of Dongyang Shen Faxing on a northern campaign; when they reached Yan Province the enemy had already gone.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming the enemy raided Yan; Emperor Xiaowu sent Heir Apparent's Guard Commandant Xue Andu and the newly appointed grand warden of Dongyang Shen Faxing north, but by the time they reached Yan the enemy had gone.

sentences.zh: 坦建議：「任榛亡命，屢犯邊民，軍出無功，宜因此翦撲。

translations.literal: Tan proposed: "The outlaw Ren Zhen has repeatedly violated border people; the army went out without achievement—it is fitting to take this opportunity to cut him down and destroy him."
translations.idiomatic: Tan proposed, "The outlaw Ren Zhen has repeatedly preyed on border people while our campaign achieved nothing; we should use this opportunity to destroy him."

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 亡命先已聞知，舉村逃走，安都與法系坐白衣領職，坦棄市。

translations.literal: The outlaw had already heard beforehand; whole villages fled; Andu and Faxing were punished by serving in plain clothes while retaining office; Tan was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhen had already heard and whole villages fled; Andu and Faxing were demoted to plain-clothes service while Tan was sentenced to execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 群臣為之請，莫能得。

translations.literal: The ministers pleaded for him, but none could obtain pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers pleaded for him in vain.

sentences.zh: 將行刑，始興公沈慶之入市抱坦慟哭曰：「卿無罪，為朝廷所枉誅，我入市亦當不久。

translations.literal: As execution was about to be carried out, Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi entered the marketplace, embraced Tan, and wailed: "You are guiltless and are wrongly executed by the court; my entering the marketplace will not be long either."
translations.idiomatic: As the execution was about to proceed, Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi entered the marketplace, embraced Tan, and wept, "You are innocent and wrongly killed by the court; I too shall not be long for this marketplace."

sentences.zh: 」市官以白上，乃原生命，繫尚方。

translations.literal: " The marketplace official reported this to the Emperor, and he then spared Tan's life and imprisoned him in the Imperial Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: The market official reported this to the Emperor, who spared Tan's life and imprisoned him in the Imperial Workshops.

sentences.zh: 尋被宥，復為驍騎將軍，病卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was pardoned, again made Valiant Cavalry General, and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon pardoned, restored as Valiant Cavalry General, and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子令孫，前廢帝景和中，為永嘉王子仁左軍司馬、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: His son Lingsun, in the Jinghe era under the Former Deposed Emperor, was Left Army staff officer to Prince of Yongjia Ziren and Grand Warden of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lingsun, in the Jinghe era under the Former Deposed Emperor, served as Left Army staff officer to Prince of Yongjia Ziren and grand warden of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 太宗以為寧朔將軍、徐州刺史，討薛安都。

translations.literal: The Taizong appointed him General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou to campaign against Xue Andu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming made him General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Xuzhou to campaign against Xue Andu.

sentences.zh: 行至淮陽，即與安都合。

translations.literal: When he reached Huaiyang he at once joined Andu.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Huaiyang, he at once joined Andu.

sentences.zh: 弟闡，時為濟陰太守，戍睢陵城，奉順不同安都，安都攻圍不能克。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chan was at the time Grand Warden of Jiyin, garrisoning Suiling city; he submitted in obedience and would not follow Andu, and Andu besieged him without being able to take him.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Chan, then grand warden of Jiyin, held Suiling in loyalty to the throne and refused to join Andu, whom Andu besieged without success.

sentences.zh: 會令孫至，遣往睢陵令說闡降，闡既降，殺之，令孫亦見殺。

translations.literal: When Lingsun arrived he was sent to Suiling to persuade Chan to surrender; once Chan had surrendered he was killed, and Lingsun was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingsun arrived he was sent to persuade Chan to surrender; once Chan yielded he was killed, and Lingsun was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 先是，清河崔諲亦以將吏見知高祖，永初末，為振威將軍、東萊太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Yin of Qinghe was also known to the Gaozu as a military officer; at the end of Yongchu he was General Who Quells Prestige and Grand Warden of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Yin of Qinghe had also been known to Emperor Wu as a military officer; at the end of Yongchu he was General Who Quells Prestige and grand warden of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 少帝初，亡命司馬靈期、司馬順之千餘人圍東萊，諲擊之，斬靈期等三十級。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Young Emperor's reign, more than a thousand outlaws under Sima Lingqi and Sima Shunzhi besieged Donglai; Yin struck them and cut off thirty heads including Lingqi's.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Young Emperor's reign more than a thousand outlaws under Sima Lingqi and Sima Shunzhi besieged Donglai; Yin attacked them and took thirty heads, including Lingqi's.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉中，至青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era under the Taizu he reached the post of Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen in Yuanjia he rose to inspector of Qing.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：漢之良吏，居官者或長子孫，孫、曹之世，善職者亦二三十載，皆敷政以盡民和，興讓以存簡久。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Han's good officials—some in office lasted through sons and grandsons; in the Sun and Cao eras, those skilled in duty also served twenty or thirty years—all spread governance to exhaust popular harmony and raised yielding to preserve simplicity and endurance.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In Han, good officials sometimes held office through sons and grandsons; in the Sun and Cao eras capable men also served twenty or thirty years, all spreading good government to harmonize the people and fostering modesty to preserve lasting simplicity.

sentences.zh: 及晚代風烈漸衰，非才有起伏，蓋所遭之時異也。

translations.literal: By the late age moral force gradually declined; it was not that talent rose and fell—probably the times they encountered were different.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages that moral force faded; it was not that talent waxed and waned, but that the times themselves had changed.

sentences.zh: 劉道產之在漢南，歷年逾十，惠化流於樊沔，頗有前世遺風，故能樹績垂名，斯為美矣！

translations.literal: Liu Daochan's stay in the south of the Han lasted more than ten years; benevolent transformation flowed through Fan and Mian, quite possessing the legacy wind of earlier ages—therefore he could establish achievements and leave a lasting name; this is beautiful indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daochan governed the Han south for more than ten years, and his benevolent rule spread through Fan and Mian with something of the old ways still in them; that is why he could win lasting achievement and fame—a thing truly admirable!
